result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content) with unsanitized RSS item content; import sets cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]; Post#cook now does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal markdown/sanitizing pipeline; best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The readability tag whitelist appears only in import_remote, not on the PollFeed path. So arbitrary HTML from the feed (including <script>) is stored verbatim as cooked content and rendered raw — stored XSS is a real defect introduced b

judged_text: PollFeed passes raw RSS item content into TopicEmbed.import, which stores it with cook_method raw_html so Post#cook returns it verbatim — feed HTML is never sanitized, because the readability tag whitelist is applied only on the sibling import_remote path. A compromised or third-party-aggregating feed injects arbitrary <script> HTML that is stored as post.cooked and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed iframe and in the normal topic view, executing on the Discourse origin for every viewer — stored XSS and session hijack.

A compromised or third-party-aggregating feed injects arbitrary <script> HTML that is stored as post.cooked and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed iframe and in the normal topic view, executing on the Discourse origin for every viewer — stored XSS and session hijack.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code takes `i.content` from the RSS (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html` posts (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). The embed rendering uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so any `<script>` or event-handler HTML from a malicious/compromised feed would be stored and rendered as-is (stored XSS on the Discourse origin). The whitelist in `import_remote` (Readability tags/attributes) does not apply to the `PollFeed` path, matching the finding.
